Consult Summary:
53-year-old male with 1-week history of painless swelling over the left elbow, clinically suggestive of olecranon bursitis. Plan for NSAID therapy, blood investigations (inflammatory and rheumatological screen), and follow-up with safety-net advice.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Left elbow swelling (possible olecranon bursitis)
- Onset: noticed ~1 week ago while showering.
- Course: Persistent; no prior episodes.
- Symptoms: Visible swelling, mild warmth; no significant pain; normal range of motion. Tender adjacent to tip, not at olecranon itself.
- Pertinent negatives: No trauma, no redness, no systemic symptoms reported.
- Examination: Visible swelling on video; skin over tip dry; mildly warm; non-tender at tip, mildly tender peri-olecranon; full movement.
- Impression: Olecranon bursitis vs other inflammatory arthropathy.
- Plan: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO BID with food (OTC; dose/route/frequency documented). Blood tests for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatology antibodies, urate. Follow-up (phone/video or face-to-face) ~6 days after blood draw. Safety-net: seek urgent review if redness, severe pain, or spreading inflammation.

Issue 2: Osteoarthritis
- History of GP-diagnosed osteoarthritis “a few years ago.” No current treatment; occasional joint pains.

Issue 3: Peanut allergy
- IgE-mediated food allergy reported; no medication allergies.

Medications:
- None regularly.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg oral twice daily after food (new recommendation).

Allergies:
- Peanuts (anaphylaxis risk not specified).
- No known drug allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis (diagnosed by GP).
- No other chronic illnesses reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: Desk-based job.
- Exercise: Runs 2–3 times/week.
- Smoking: Not documented.
- Alcohol: Not documented.
- Living situation: Not documented.

Preventative History:
- No preventive screening or vaccination information provided.

Physical Examination:
- Video inspection of left elbow: visible swelling, dry skin over olecranon, warmth compared with surrounding skin, mild peri-olecranon tenderness, full active movement.
- Vitals: Not documented.

Plan:
- Start ibuprofen 400 mg PO BID with food; stop if GI side-effects.
- Mail blood test form; patient to attend phlebotomy for:
  • Full blood count  
  • CRP/ESR  
  • Rheumatologic antibody panel  
  • Uric acid  
  • Other infection/inflammatory markers per protocol
- Arrange follow-up (video/phone or in-person) ~6 days after blood draw to review results and re-examine elbow.
- Safety-net: If elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, or swelling spreads, contact service urgently for same-day review to exclude septic arthritis.
- Provide reassurance that condition currently not life-threatening.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: smoking status, alcohol intake, medication reconciliation beyond patient’s statement, family history details, immunization & preventive screening history, vitals.
● No internal transcript conflicts detected.
● Transcript quality good; occasional minor inaudible segments but clinical content clear.
